context: Current closing price of Procter & Gamble (PG): $173.02 USD as of 2026-11-17.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish near-term bias with a relatively flat trajectory over time. At the one-day horizon, I anchored close to recent price action, assuming mean-reverting behavior and no major catalyst within the next session. The slight upward drift in the one-week and one-month estimates reflects the general tendency of equity markets to grind higher in the absence of negative shocks, as well as any residual momentum that may be present in the underlying asset. The incremental increases across horizons are intentionally small because I did not want to project a strong directional trend without clearer fundamental or technical confirmation.

Confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect how uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the tight range of roughly plus or minus 3 points reflects the relatively low expected daily volatility and the short window for new information to materially alter pricing. By one week, the range widens to about 11 points in total, incorporating the possibility of scheduled economic data releases, earnings, or Federal Reserve communications that could shift sentiment. At one month, the interval opens substantially to about 24 points, acknowledging that over a four-week period, macro conditions, sector rotations, and broader risk appetite can shift meaningfully in either direction. Historical realized volatility for assets in this price range was an important input for scaling these intervals appropriately.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside my stated ranges. On the downside, a sharper-than-expected deterioration in macroeconomic data, a surprise in central bank policy, or a geopolitical escalation could produce a move well below the lower bounds, particularly at the one-month horizon. Credit stress in financial markets or a sudden liquidity event could also trigger outsized selling. On the upside, a strongly positive earnings surprise, a dovish policy pivot, or a broad risk-on rally driven by improving global data could push prices above the upper bounds. Fat-tail events by definition are underweighted in standard confidence intervals, so I would caution that true tail outcomes remain possible even if my stated ranges suggest otherwise.
